objective: Prove: every n x m torus of rings (n, m >= 3, equally spaced law-(12,12) contacts) has a half-turn fixing each contact and exchanging its rings, so every contact persists at every lag; hence growth by inserting a band of rings round the torus, or by splitting every ring into a k x l block, keeps every contact persistent at every stage. Attaching a single new ring by one contact gives a return of length 1; by two contacts that are not consecutive on one ring, an unpaired return of length 2; and as a bubble (two consecutive contacts on one ring) it deletes that ring's corner, which by the Sherman-Morrison formula breaks persistence at its tail whenever its head reaches its tail.
status: Proved 2026-11-08 (by hand; finite claims checked exactly): every n x m torus of equally spaced rings (n, m >= 3) has a half-turn at every contact, so every contact persists and growth by inserting bands or splitting every ring into blocks keeps every contact persistent at every stage; attaching one new ring breaks persistence by one contact (a return of length 1), by two contacts not forming a bubble (an unpaired return of length 2), and as a bubble on p -> q exactly when some old contact is reached from q and reaches p (D'_cc = 1 + w D_cq D_pc / (1 + w D_pq)).
title: Bands grow, single rings do not
